sources.symbol: Envelope & Oneof Payload Dispatch
sources.summary: Root wire container wrapping protocol_version, request_id correlation, and the 18-branch oneof payload.
sources.explanation: Every TCP frame decodes into a single `chat.protocol.Envelope`. Tag 1 (`protocol_version`) must be `1`. Tag 2 (`request_id`) correlates client requests with their direct `Ack`/`Error`/`Response` replies, while unsolicited server pushes (`DirectMessage`, `GroupMessage`, `UserListUpdate`, `GroupListUpdate`) leave `request_id` empty. Tags 10–21 cover core chat/presence/heartbeat/ack/error; tags 30–35 cover Stage 8–11 durability (history, sequence sync, and private room discovery).
sources.risk: If `protocol_version != 1` or `payload_case() == PAYLOAD_NOT_SET` is not checked before dispatch, a blank or future-version packet could be misinterpreted as a default action.

sources.symbol: encode_frame() — Big-Endian Header Serialization
sources.summary: Validates payload size (1..1 MiB) and prepends the 4-byte network-order length.
sources.explanation: Checks `payload.empty()` and `payload.size() > kMaxFrameSize`. Reserves `4 + payload.size()` bytes up front (single heap allocation), then shifts the 32-bit unsigned size by 24, 16, 8, and 0 bits masked with `0xffU` to produce big-endian (MSB-first) bytes regardless of whether the host CPU is little-endian (x86_64/ARM).
sources.risk: Writing raw `memcpy(&size, ...)` would send little-endian bytes on x86, breaking network byte order.

sources.symbol: FrameDecoder::feed() — Incremental Stream State Machine
sources.summary: Consumes an arbitrary chunk of TCP bytes, assembling 4-byte headers and N-byte payloads across splits or coalesced packets.
sources.explanation: In a `while (offset < bytes.size())` loop: Phase 1 fills `header_` up to 4 bytes using `std::min(4 - header_size_, bytes.size() - offset)`. If fewer than 4 header bytes have arrived so far, it breaks and waits for the next TCP read. Once all 4 header bytes arrive, it reconstructs `payload_size_` via bit shifts, validates `1 <= payload_size_ <= max_frame_size_`, and calls `payload_.reserve(payload_size_)`. Phase 2 copies up to `remaining = payload_size_ - payload_.size()` bytes into `payload_`. When `payload_.size() == payload_size_`, the completed frame is `std::move`d into `frames` and state resets (`header_size_ = 0`, `payload_size_ = 0`) to immediately parse any coalesced next frame in the same buffer.
sources.risk: If `header_size_` and `payload_` weren't preserved as member variables across `feed()` calls, any frame split across two `async_read_some` calls would corrupt the stream.

sources.symbol: FrameDecoder::finish() — Clean vs Truncated EOF Check
sources.summary: Called when TCP read returns `eof` to detect mid-frame disconnection.
sources.explanation: Note that when `header_size_ == 4`, `payload_size_` is non-zero until the payload finishes (at which point `header_size_` resets to `0`). Therefore `header_size_ != 0U` catches BOTH a partial 1–3 byte header AND a complete 4-byte header whose payload has not finished arriving!
sources.risk: Without `finish()`, a half-closed socket that sent half a frame would be treated as a clean EOF instead of a protocol truncation error.

sources.symbol: void verify_tls_peer(
send(), stop() & stop_on_executor() (Bounded Admission & Abortive Close)
sources.summary: Serializes Envelope into a framed shared_ptr buffer, checks 256-frame / 2-MiB bounds under queue_mutex_, schedules pump_write() once, and handles idempotent teardown.
sources.explanation: In `send()`: 1) Serializes and encodes the frame outside the lock. 2) Locks `queue_mutex_`, checks `accepting_sends_`, and checks `queue_.size() >= limits_.queued_frames || frame->size() > limits_.queued_bytes - queued_bytes_` (using subtraction so `queued_bytes_ + frame->size()` cannot integer-overflow!). 3) If `pump_scheduled_` is false, sets it to true and posts `pump_write()` to `executor_`. In `stop_on_executor()`: cancels `idle_timer_`, clears `queue_`, closes `stream_.socket()` abortively, and invokes `on_close_(*this)` exactly once.
sources.risk: Calling `async_shutdown` on TLS during `stop_on_executor()` would launch a second concurrent writer on `ssl::stream` while `async_write` is in flight (undefined behavior in Boost.Asio SSL) and let a dead peer hang teardown.

sources.symbol: wait_for_idle() — Timestamp-Based Lazy Idle Timer
sources.summary: Expires silent connections after 30s without cancelling/re-arming the kernel timer on every incoming message.
sources.explanation: Instead of calling `idle_timer_.expires_after(30s)` inside `read()` on every message (which would force Asio to cancel and re-post a timer operation for every single chat message!), `read()` merely updates `last_activity_ = steady_clock::now()`. When `idle_timer_` wakes up, it checks if `now() >= last_activity_ + idle_timeout`: if yes, it closes the session; if traffic arrived in the meantime, it sleeps for the remaining time (`expires_at(last_activity_ + idle_timeout)`).
sources.risk: Rearming `steady_timer` on every frame in a high-throughput chat room would flood the strand with `operation_aborted` timer completions.

sources.symbol: read() — Incremental Frame Decoding, Half-Close Drain & Envelope Validation
sources.summary: Reads up to 4096 bytes into `input_`, feeds `decoder_`, validates `Envelope` v1, updates `last_activity_`, and dispatches `on_message_`.
sources.explanation: Look at the EOF handling (lines 171–188): if the peer performs a TCP half-close (`shutdown(SD_SEND)` -> `error == eof`) right after sending a valid request, `decoder_.finish()` succeeds, `read_closed_` becomes `true`, and if `queue_` is non-empty, `read()` returns WITHOUT calling `stop_on_executor()` so `pump_write()` can finish draining the queued reply before closing the socket (line 231)!
sources.risk: If `eof` immediately closed the socket while `queue_` still held the `Pong` or `Ack` for the final request, clients doing send-then-half-close would lose their response.

sources.symbol: login() — Unique Username Reservation & Durable Identity Verification (R3, R4)
sources.summary: Rejects re-login, invalid names, or taken usernames; verifies/issues durable `resume_token` via HistoryStore; broadcasts user & group snapshots.
sources.explanation: Checks: 1) `!connection.username.empty()` (cannot rename an already logged-in connection), 2) `!valid_username(name)`, 3) `usernames_.contains(name)` (R3 uniqueness). If `storage_` is active, calls `storage_->identity(name, resume_token)` to either create a new principal + 256-bit token or verify an existing token's SHA-256 hash. Sends `LoginResponse` FIRST (line 223), then calls `broadcast(true, true)` (line 225) so the client always receives its `LoginResponse` before `UserListUpdate` and `GroupListUpdate`!
sources.risk: Reserving `usernames_.emplace(...)` before `storage_->identity(...)` succeeds would leak a locked username if the database threw an error or rejected an invalid resume token.

sources.symbol: direct() — Pair-Scoped Direct Rooms & Private Routing (R5, R7)
sources.summary: Validates DM fields, rejects forged metadata, checks retry cache, commits to SQLite, sends ACK, and delivers ONLY to sender and recipient.
sources.explanation: Lines 231–235 enforce strict anti-spoofing: `!message.sender().empty() || !message.room_id().empty() || !message.message_id().empty() || message.room_sequence() != 0 || message.server_timestamp_unix_ms() != 0` all trigger `INVALID_REQUEST`. Next, `retry()` checks if `client_message_id` was already accepted for this sender—if so, it re-sends the original `Ack` even if the recipient has since gone offline! Otherwise it looks up `recipient` in `usernames_`, commits via `storage_->direct(...)` (or assigns ephemeral `direct-N` for `Pair{min(id1,id2), max(id1,id2)}`), sends `Ack` to `session`, sends `delivery` echo to `session`, and sends `delivery` to `recipient_session` (if not a self-DM).
sources.risk: Notice `auto recipient_session = recipient.session;` is copied to a local `shared_ptr` before `session.send()` in case `session` disconnects.

sources.symbol: create_group(), join_group() & group_message() — Voluntary Groups (R8, R10, R11)
sources.summary: Creates groups with creator-only membership (R8), processes explicit self-join by group_id (R10), and routes group messages exclusively to current members (R11).
sources.explanation: In `create_group()`: validates `valid_group_name(name)` and `groups_.size() < 128`, creates `group-N` in SQLite or memory, inserts `{&session}` as the sole initial member, sends `Ack`, and broadcasts `GroupListUpdate`. In `join_group()`: checks `groups_.find(id)` and `!members.contains(&session)`, records audit admission in SQLite, inserts `&session`, sends `Ack`, and broadcasts `GroupListUpdate`. In `group_message()`: verifies `found->second.members.contains(&session)` (`NOT_GROUP_MEMBER` if not), checks retry deduplication, commits message, sends `Ack`, and iterates ONLY over `found->second.members` to send the `GroupMessage` delivery!
sources.risk: Checking membership after `retry()` in `group_message()` would allow a former member who disconnected and reconnected without rejoining to replay group retries.

sources.symbol: RAII Statement, Transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), SHA-256 Hashing & Room ID Parser
sources.summary: Wraps `sqlite3_stmt` and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`ROLLBACK` in exception-safe RAII classes; implements OpenSSL EVP_sha256 token hashing and strict `direct-N`/`group-N` number parsing.
sources.explanation: `Statement` calls `sqlite3_prepare_v2` in its constructor and `sqlite3_finalize` in its destructor, binding strings with `SQLITE_TRANSIENT` (forcing SQLite to make its own internal copy immediately). `Transaction` executes `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (acquiring a write lock immediately on start so mid-transaction `SQLITE_BUSY` deadlocks cannot occur) and automatically runs `ROLLBACK` in `~Transaction()` unless `commit()` succeeded. `token_hash()` hashes the 64-hex resume token with `EVP_sha256()` so a leaked database file never exposes usable bearer tokens!
sources.risk: Using `BEGIN DEFERRED` instead of `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` can cause two concurrent readers upgrading to writers to deadlock mid-transaction without waiting for the 100ms `busy_timeout`.

sources.symbol: identity(), groups(), create_group(), join_group(), direct(), group_message() & retry()
sources.summary: Implements durable principal creation/verification, atomic room/message commits, and sender-scoped retry deduplication.
sources.explanation: In `identity(name, token)`: if `token` is empty, generates a fresh 256-bit token and inserts a new row into `users(name, token_hash)`—even if `name` was used in the past! That guarantees a new user claiming `"Alice"` gets a brand-new `principal` ID and cannot read the previous `"Alice"`'s direct messages! In `direct()` and `group_message()`: both start a `Transaction`, check `retry()` inside the transaction, insert the message + advance `last_sequence` via `append()`, and call `transaction.commit()`. In `retry()`: looks up `(principal, client_key)` and verifies that `kind`, `target`, and `text` match the original message, throwing `MessageIdConflict` if any differ.
sources.risk: Checking `retry()` outside the write transaction would allow a race condition if two identical retries arrived back-to-back.

sources.symbol: direct_participant(), history(), sync() & direct_rooms()
sources.summary: Implements bounded cursor pagination (`LIMIT limit + 1`), contiguous sequence verification for `sync()`, and principal-scoped direct room discovery.
sources.explanation: Notice the pagination trick in `history()` (line 373) and `direct_rooms()` (line 454): it binds `LIMIT limit + 1`! If `limit + 1` rows come back, it stops after adding `limit` entries and sets `has_more = true` without needing a separate `SELECT COUNT(*)` query! In `sync()` (lines 391–440): if `through == 0`, it captures `through = latest` (`rooms.last_sequence`) as the fixed upper watermark. As it reads rows ordered by `sequence`, line 422 checks `if (sequence != result.next_sequence() + 1) throw std::invalid_argument("sync gap")`—if any row was deleted or corrupted in the database, the server immediately reports `ERROR_CODE_SYNC_GAP` instead of silently skipping a message!
sources.risk: Without the contiguous `sequence == next_sequence + 1` check in `sync()`, a database gap would cause the client cursor to jump over missing messages without warning.

sources.symbol: PingClient (`ChatClient`) Blocking Operations API
sources.summary: Declares deadline-bounded `connect`, `ping`, `login`, `resume_login`, `history`, `sync`, `direct_rooms`, `send_direct[_with_key]`, `create_group`, `join_group`, `send_group[_with_key]`, `next_event`, and `close`.
sources.explanation: Every network method takes an explicit `std::chrono::milliseconds timeout = std::chrono::seconds(3)`. `next_event()` uses a *soft* deadline: if no event arrives within `timeout`, it cancels the read and returns `std::nullopt` while keeping the TCP/TLS connection and any partial `FrameDecoder` bytes intact!
sources.risk: If `next_event()` closed the socket on timeout like `exchange()` does, polling for incoming chat messages every 25ms would disconnect the client after 35ms!

sources.symbol: event(), receive() & exchange() — Two-Phase Event Loop & Interleaved Buffering
sources.summary: The heart of `PingClient`: writes the request frame using `run_one()`, then reads frames until the matching `request_id` arrives while buffering unsolicited events in `events_`.
sources.explanation: Look at `exchange()` (lines 467–502): why does it run `while (!written && failure_.empty()) { context_.run_one(); }` for the `async_write`, and then call `receive(response, &outgoing)` which calls `context_.run()`? Because the `timer_` is ALREADY armed on `context_`! If `exchange()` called `context_.run()` right after `async_write`, `context_.run()` would block until `timer_` also finished (3 full seconds!) because `timer_.async_wait` is outstanding work on `context_`! Instead, `run_one()` steps one completion at a time until `written == true` (while `timer_` stays live!), and then `receive()` starts `async_read_some` and calls `complete({})` when the response arrives, which cancels `timer_` so `context_.run()` returns immediately!
sources.risk: Calling `context_.run()` after `async_write` without cancelling `timer_` would make every single `send_direct` block for the full 3-second timeout before even starting to read the reply!

sources.symbol: run() Lambdas: `publish`, `track`, `replay`, `dispatch` & `synchronize`
sources.summary: Implements per-room sequence tracking (up to 256 rooms), live gap detection, and fixed-watermark multi-page sequence catch-up.
sources.explanation: Look at `dispatch()` (lines 210–242): when a live `DirectDelivery` or `GroupDelivery` arrives with `sequence`, it compares `sequence` against `cursor.sequence`: 1) If `sequence <= cursor.sequence`, it is a duplicate of a message already replayed during `sync()`—so it is silently suppressed (line 228)! 2) If `sequence > cursor.sequence + 1`, a live gap occurred—so it calls `replay(id, cursor, sequence - 1)` BEFORE publishing the live event! Look at `synchronize()` (lines 243–272): after reconnecting and rejoining `wanted_groups`, it pages `client.direct_rooms()`, drains up to 256 buffered login/join snapshots (`next_event(1ms)`) so `RoomModel` knows about groups BEFORE group messages replay, and then calls `replay(id, cursor)` for every tracked room!
sources.risk: If `synchronize()` replayed group messages before draining the `GroupSnapshot` emitted by `join_group()`, `RoomModel::apply()` would throw `"group delivery precedes discovery"`!

sources.symbol: Initial Connect/Login, Recovery Loop (`resume_login` + Rejoin) & Heartbeat Cadence
sources.summary: Performs initial login (saving `token = login.resume_token`), handles exponential-backoff reconnect (`250ms -> 500ms -> 1000ms -> 2000ms -> 2500ms`), and sends 10s Pings.
sources.explanation: When `recovering == true` (lines 291–332): checks `attempts == limits_.reconnect_attempts` (16), publishes `WorkerReconnecting`, sleeps via `wake_.wait_for(lock, stop, delay, ...)` (which wakes instantly if `stop` is requested!), doubles `delay` up to `2500ms`, connects, calls `client.resume_login(username, token)`, and if the server says `"username is already connected"` (because the server hasn't noticed the old half-open TCP socket died yet!), throws `NetworkError` so the worker keeps retrying until the old session expires! Then it rejoins `wanted_groups`, runs `synchronize()`, and publishes `WorkerConnected{username, true}` (`resumed = true`).
sources.risk: If `"username is already connected"` during `resume_login` threw `std::runtime_error` instead of `NetworkError`, a brief Wi-Fi blip where the client reconnects faster than the server's 30s idle timer would permanently kill the client session!

sources.symbol: apply(const ClientEvent&) — Snapshot & Delivery Router
sources.summary: Updates `users_` and `groups_` from server snapshots and routes `DirectDelivery` and `GroupDelivery` into their isolated `RoomView`s (R5).
sources.explanation: On `UserSnapshot`: updates `users_` and marks any direct room whose `target` is no longer in `users_` as `available = false`. That single line (`room.available = false`, line 156) guarantees that if Bob disconnects and a new Bob logs in, `open_direct("Bob")` (which searches for `room.available == true`) will create a brand-new `direct-view-2` instead of reusing `direct-view-1`! On `GroupSnapshot`: creates or updates `group:group-N` views and sets `found->joined = contains(group.members, username_)`. On `DirectDelivery`: matches existing `wire_id == direct->room_id`, or binds an available provisional view for `peer`, or creates a new view, then calls `append()`.
sources.risk: Reusing an old direct view after a peer disconnects in ephemeral mode would mix two different sessions' conversations.

sources.symbol: parse_command() — `/help`, `/users`, `/groups`, `/members`, `/dm`, `/create`, `/join`, `/group`, `/quit`
sources.summary: Validates command syntax, target bounds (1–64B), and text bounds (1–4096B) before touching the worker.
sources.explanation: Rejects any ASCII control characters (except `'\t'` whitespace) and enforces exact argument counts: `/help`, `/users`, `/groups`, `/quit` take 0 args; `/members` and `/join` take 1 target arg; `/create` takes the rest of the line (1–64B) as the group name (allowing spaces like `/create Study Group`); `/dm` and `/group` take a target token followed by 1–4096B of message text.
sources.risk: Using `token(line)` for `/create` would forbid spaces in group names.

sources.symbol: Dependencies, protoc Custom Command, `chat_proto`, `chat_framing` & Warning Function
sources.code:
VERBATIM
)

# Consumers inherit generated-header and dependency include paths from targets.
add_library(chat_proto STATIC "${CHAT_PROTO_SOURCE}" "${CHAT_PROTO_HEADER}")
add_library(chat::proto ALIAS chat_proto)
target_compile_features(chat_proto PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
target_include_directories(chat_proto PUBLIC "${CHAT_GENERATED_DIR}")
target_link_libraries(chat_proto PUBLIC protobuf::libprotobuf)

add_library(chat_framing STATIC src/protocol/framing.cpp)
add_library(chat::framing ALIAS chat_framing)
target_compile_features(chat_framing PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
target_include_directories(chat_framing PUBLIC "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include")
sources.summary: Finds Protobuf, Boost.Asio, Threads, SQLite3, OpenSSL; generates `chat.pb.cc/.h` via `protobuf::protoc`; defines `chat_proto` and `chat_framing`.
sources.explanation: `add_custom_command` runs `protobuf::protoc` whenever `proto/chat.proto` changes, outputting into `build/<preset>/generated/`. `chat_framing` links ONLY standard C++20 (`include/`), proving the frame codec has zero socket or Protobuf dependencies.
sources.risk: Applying `/W4` or `-Wextra` directly to `chat_proto` would fail or flood the build with warnings inside protoc-generated C++ code.

files.role: Defines the strongly-typed binary application message contract (Envelope + 18 payload types) compiled by protoc into chat.pb.h and chat.pb.cc.
Declares the 1 MiB frame limit, FrameError exception, encode_frame(), and the stateful FrameDecoder incremental byte-stream parser.
Implements 4-byte big-endian length encoding and incremental state-machine frame extraction across arbitrary TCP read boundaries.
Provides inline validation for client retry keys (`valid_message_key`), declares 256-bit random key generation (`new_message_key`), and computes server Unix millisecond timestamps.
Generates 32 cryptographically random bytes via OpenSSL RAND_bytes and encodes them as a 64-character lowercase hex string.
Declares TlsError, ClientTlsOptions (CA bundle + expected SAN), and ServerTlsOptions (cert chain + private key + handshake timeout) without exposing OpenSSL or Boost.Asio headers.
Wraps either a plain `boost::asio::ip::tcp::socket` (loopback dev mode) or a `boost::asio::ssl::stream<tcp::socket>` (TLS 1.3 mode) behind one unified async_read_some / async_write_some interface.
Configures OpenSSL SSL_CTX to enforce TLS 1.3 only, loads server cert/key or client CA bundle, and binds strict DNS/IP Subject Alternative Name (SAN) verification.
Parses `--tls <CA-file> [--server-name <DNS/IP>]` or `--plaintext-dev` for `chat_cli` and `chat_gui`, rejecting missing or mixed transport flags.
Parses server CLI arguments (`--tls` or `--plaintext-dev`, bind address, port, SQLite path, idle timeout), constructs PingServer, hooks SIGINT/SIGTERM, and runs the Boost.Asio io_context.
Declares the top-level server class that owns the TCP acceptor, the shared hub strand, and the authoritative ChatHub.
Binds the listening socket, enforces the 64-connection cap, creates ClientSessions bound to the shared hub strand, and posts session removal onto the strand.
Declares per-connection state: SocketStream, FrameDecoder, 4 KiB read buffer, mutex-guarded bounded write queue (256 frames / 2 MiB), and steady_timer idle expiry (30s).

Implements the server's per-client async state machine: TLS 1.3 server handshake with deadline, mutex-ordered write admission, single-writer pump, half-close EOF draining, and low-overhead idle timeout.
Declares the central server state machine: active connections, unique usernames map, direct rooms, groups, ephemeral retry cache, and HistoryStore pointer.
Implements all server business rules (R3–R11), anti-spoofing validation, retry deduplication, commit-before-ACK routing, and presence/group snapshot broadcasts.
Declares StoredIdentity, StoredGroup, StoredMessage, MessageIdConflict, and the HistoryStore class wrapping SQLite3.

Manages SQLite3 connection in WAL + synchronous=FULL mode, RAII prepared statements and BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions, SHA-256 resume tokens, atomic v1->v2 schema upgrade, deduplicated message insertion, and watermark sync.
Aliases `chat::client::ChatClient = PingClient` so application code uses the descriptive name while keeping Stage 2 PingClient compatibility.

Declares all GUI-independent client structs (`LoginResult`, `OperationResult`, `ClientEvent` variant, `HistoryPage`, `SyncPage`, `DirectRoomsPage`, `NetworkError`) and the blocking `PingClient` (`ChatClient`) class.
Implements PingClient::Impl using an internal Boost.Asio io_context, driving async_resolve/connect/handshake/write/read synchronously with a steady_timer deadline while buffering unsolicited events.
Declares the multi-threaded bridge between the non-blocking UI/CLI presentation thread and the blocking `ChatClient` networking thread (`std::jthread`).
Implements the worker thread lifecycle: connect/login, 10s heartbeat Pings, command execution with pre-assigned retry keys, 25ms event polling, and Stage 11 automatic reconnect + sequence replay.
Declares the pure-C++ UI state model (`ChatLine`, `RoomView`, `RoomModel`) that manages room navigation, drafts, transcripts, and sequence deduplication without any Win32 dependencies.
Implements room creation/eviction, provisional-to-wire room binding, sequence duplicate suppression, global LRU line trimming, and non-destructive draft management.

Supports two modes in one binary: 1) Persistent interactive chat (`chat_cli <tls-mode> chat <host> <port> <username>`) using `ChatConsole` + `ConsoleInput`, and 2) One-shot diagnostic Ping/login (`chat_cli <tls-mode> <host> <port> [nonce] [username]`).
Declares `InputChunk` and the cross-platform `ConsoleInput` class that polls terminal keystrokes, pipes, or redirected files without blocking.

Implements non-blocking stdin reads for Windows consoles (`ReadConsoleInputW` with UTF-16 surrogate pair assembly), Windows pipes (`PeekNamedPipe`), Windows files, and POSIX descriptors (`::poll` + `::read`).
Declares `escape_text`, `LineInput` (incremental 8 KiB line accumulator with UTF-8 backspace), `parse_command`, and `ChatConsole`.

Implements terminal-injection escaping (`escape_text`), incremental CRLF/UTF-8 backspace line assembly (`LineInput`), `/command` parsing, and `ChatWorker` event presentation + 5-second quit receipt draining.
Parses wide-character Windows command line (`CommandLineToArgvW`), validates `--tls` or `--plaintext-dev`, creates the native `chat::gui::Window`, and runs the Win32 message loop.
Declares stable `ControlId` enum values (used by both layout/command handlers and automated GUI tests) and the `Window` class owning `ChatWorker` and `RoomModel`.

Implements UTF-8 <-> UTF-16 conversion (with embedded NUL visualization), Win32 control creation/layout, 40ms timer polling (`WM_TIMER` -> `pump()`), non-flickering transcript/draft refresh, and `WndProc` dispatch.
Defines the dependency graph (`chat_proto` -> `chat_framing` -> `chat_shared` -> `chat_transport` -> `chat_cli_view`/`chat_gui_view` -> executables & 3 CTest suites) and ASAN/UBSAN flags.
